A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeSubNet research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching renamed and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-cancer network evaluations, gene-knockout simulations, biological enrichment analyses, case studies, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements and a Pan-Cancer scalability evaluation in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The VQ-VAE Patient-M, Neo-GNN Graph-M, and Infer-M retain the same architecture, three training phases, parameter freezing, and objectives in Equations (1)–(3). Naming corrections and Figure 2 revisions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds TCGA Pan-Cancer expression data with 8,314 patients, evaluated using the BRCA graph for computational scaling. The original BRCA, GBM, LGG, and OV coverage remains; no Pan-Cancer network-quality or biological-validation results are added.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain WGCNA, wTO, ARACNe, LEAP, GAERF, LR-GNN, and CSGNN, including the same selected subsets in Figures 3 and 5. Appendix C.1 adds selection rationale without changing comparator membership; the ablation variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Appendix E evaluation measures training time, inference time, and GPU memory, including the 8,314-patient Pan-Cancer test with the BRCA graph. Existing preprocessing, dataset sizes, graph metrics, and hyperparameter settings remain unchanged. The newly specified GO Biological Process category documents previously unspecified scope rather than establishing a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a supplementary analysis of computational requirements and scalability to a larger patient cohort. Existing module ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, knockout simulations, BRCA case studies, and prior-versus-generated graph analysis are retained, including Figures 7 and 8.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 contains only point estimates; v3 introduces ± uncertainty quantities throughout the central four-cancer comparison and also reports them in the new computational-cost table. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, but neither their statistical meaning nor associated run counts or seeds is specified. Additional experimental repetitions therefore cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports computational results, including Pan-Cancer training time of 454.47 seconds, inference time of 142.86 seconds, and GPU memory usage of 15,893 MB. All 96 Table 2 point estimates remain identical, as do enrichment results, the 0.83/0.12 knockout shift rates, sensitivity results, and ablation findings.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, graph hypotheses, training equations, Shift Rate formulation, and appendix metric definitions retain their mathematical substance. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same subtype-network inference proposal, four-cancer performance claims, biological relevance claims, and dataset contribution. The conclusion is rephrased, but the central scientific claims and their scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix E interprets resource measurements as supporting practical feasibility and scalability. Appendix G.1 adds substantive rationale connecting Biological Process terms to cancer mechanisms and therapeutic targets. Existing explanations of biological results and the difficulty of OV remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 updates the reported code/data location from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository, explicitly identifies the GO Biological Process scope, and supplies training/inference time and memory measurements. Hardware specifications and precise timing procedures remain unspecified; existing preprocessing instructions and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting GO interpretation and biological background, including Desmedt, Shapiro, and Ashkenazi, plus clusterProfiler 4.0 and a newer KEGG paper. Appendix C.1 explains baseline selection. The main positioning against statistical and GNN methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes the GeSubNet name, edits wording and author information, adds acknowledgments, and introduces appendix subsections explaining baseline selection and GO categories. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with equation references and a revised caption, inconsistent method labels are corrected, Table 2 becomes denser with ± entries, and a computational-cost table is added. Existing displays are resized or relocated, including Figure 7; these are localized changes rather than an overall visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves practical assessment and clarity through the new computational-cost evaluation, explicit GO scope, baseline-selection rationale, and clearer method labeling. However, undefined ± quantities and missing hardware/timing details limit the value of the added reporting. The central method and existing empirical findings remain unchanged.
